runners.comment: 6l second to Proactif at Auteuil (2m2f, very soft) when green; could be a big improver
runners.name: Apolon De Charnie
runners.spotlight: Last of six in a 1m4f French Flat maiden in August, but second of 18 in newcomers hurdle race at Auteuil (2m2f, very soft) in September when beaten 6l by Proactif who is now his stablemate; jumped in green fashion that day but passed seven of his rivals in the home straight; could be a big improver but a bit more experience would have been preferable.

runners.comment: 15l fourth of five in Naas Listed race does not suggest any threat to today's principals
runners.name: Berto Ramirez
runners.owner: D OMahony & D McHugh & D J Kelly & G Butler
runners.spotlight: Placed only once from 12 starts on the Flat, showing fair form at best; big odds for his three races in the mud over hurdles, appearing to show his best form when fourth of five in Listed race at Naas last time, but that 15l defeat does not suggest any threat to today's principals.

runners.comment: 1m6f Listed winner on Flat; he hasn't made a serious impact in either of his hurdle races
runners.name: Fantasy World
runners.spotlight: 1m6f Listed winner on Flat who was sold for 600,000gns later in October; flopped at long odds-on for hurdling debut at Musselburgh last month; brought out just six days later for Grade 2 at Kempton (again good to soft) where he did better, but was weakening when hampered two out; should get the hang of this discipline in due course, but probably too late to feature in this finish.

runners.comment: Needs much better than when 4th to Macho Man at Auteuil (favourite) but has joined Mullins
runners.name: Forty Fifty
runners.spotlight: 102,000euros 2yo; half-brother to two French Flat winners; dam French 1m5f winner, half-sister to French Group 1 winners Full Of Gold (1m2f) and Fuisse (1m); favourite for newcomers hurdle race at Auteuil (2m2f, very soft) in October, but in rear at halfway before plugging on into fourth of 14 to Macho Man; needs much better than that display but he's joined Mullins.

runners.breeder: Airlie Stud & Mrs S M Rogers
runners.comment: 3-3 over hurdles in the north but this race is a vastly harder task
runners.name: Indian River
runners.spotlight: Promise in his two Irish Flat maidens; justified favouritism in juvenile hurdles at Catterick (good) and Wetherby (soft) and a seven-runner handicap against older horses at Sedgefield (good to soft); won latest with more authority than 2l margin suggests, but this race is a vastly harder task; failed to make the cut for the 4yo handicap here on Tuesday.

runners.comment: French Flat win; won hurdle debut at Naas (heavy) when front-running didn't seem the plan
runners.name: Kai Lung
runners.spotlight: In the first three in his six Flat starts in France, with sole win over 7.5f but also a 1m2f second on final outing; 6-1 and hooded for 12-runner maiden at Naas (heavy) in January, whereas Mon Creuset (blundered two out) was the evens favourite, but this one made all (slow pace initially) for a 2l win with Tuesday's Festival winner Saratoga in third; those tactics did not seem to be the plan at all, with settling a major issue, yet he found plenty for pressure and it was a promising introduction.

runners.comment: 17l defeat at Kelso Grade 2 (2m2f, good to soft) 13 days ago does not augur well
runners.name: Lord Byron
runners.spotlight: Ran twice on Flat for Aidan O'Brien; three hurdle races this winter, a never-dangerous 4l fourth to Maestro Conti in Grade 2 Triumph Trial at Cheltenham (2m1f, soft) on second occasion; first-time cheekpieces in Kelso Grade 2 (2m2f, good to soft) 13 days ago where a 17l defeat does not augur well for this.

runners.comment: Showed his inexperience when 2nd to Proactif and could be more polished following that run
runners.name: Macho Man
runners.spotlight: Comfortable winner at Auteuil (2m2f, very soft) in October in his only French race; narrowly favourite from Proactif in eight-runner race at Fairyhouse (yielding) two months ago on Irish debut but had to settle for second behind that stablemate, beaten nearly 3l having chased the leaders but disputed the lead at the final flight; showed his inexperience and could be more polished with the benefit of that run.

runners.comment: 3-3, latest run at this track; more to do but it's hard to say just how good he might be
runners.name: Maestro Conti
runners.spotlight: Untroubled to win his sole start in France (heavy) and the same at Kempton (good) on British debut; came to the fore in tidy style on run-in for Grade 2 here (soft) seven weeks ago, going past One Horse Town having been short of room and hugged the near-side rail; should have much more to do in this race but it's hard to say just how good he might be.

runners.comment: Sold for £370,000 six days after winning a weak Cork race (4-5) in November; major promise
runners.name: Minella Academy
runners.spotlight: Flat pedigree, with dam a half-sister to 1m Group/Grade 1 winner Aussie Rules; unraced in that sphere but made 4-5 for 12-runner juvenile hurdle at Cork (2m1f, yielding to soft) in November, making all and seeing off the only serious challenger before left clear; followed that run for John Nallen with a £370,000 sale six days later and brings major promise to this first outing for Mullins, albeit moving from a weak race to the best in the division.

runners.comment: 3-3 hurdling; latest (C&D) made him the highest-rated runner in this from a British stable
runners.name: Minella Study
runners.spotlight: Ordinary maiden on the Flat; won hurdling debut at Tipperary in July, however, and has emerged as a leading juvenile hurdler for new yard with his Listed win at Wetherby (good; overcame a bad late mistake) and Triumph Trial win over C&D (good to soft; by just over 6l from Winston Junior); the latter makes him the highest-rated runner in this from a British stable.

runners.comment: 4th to Kai Lung at Naas (heavy) but was evens and travelling strongly before blunder 2 out
runners.name: Mon Creuset
runners.spotlight: Made most to win a 1m4f bumper at Nantes last October; beaten nearly 9l behind stablemate Kai Lung in maiden hurdle at Naas (heavy) in January but was evens favourite and challenged two out, travelling strongly, only to make a bad mistake; capable of markedly better but it's hard to say how much.

runners.comment: Beaten about 11l at Leopardstown (yielding/heavy) in Gr 2 and Gr 1 won by Narciso Has
runners.name: North Shore
runners.spotlight: 1m4f winner on the first of four French Flat starts; beaten about 11l at Leopardstown (yielding/heavy) in his two hurdle races, admittedly in the Grade 2 and Grade 1 won by Narciso Has (who was a hot favourite for this race before injury) but he did not show enough to suggest he's a leading player.

runners.comment: Useful but limitations likely to be evident, as they were against Maestro Conti over C&D
runners.name: One Horse Town
runners.spotlight: Often front-runner; won his first four hurdle races and placed in three better contests since; gave 2lb when 2l second to Maestro Conti in Grade 2 over C&D on penultimate outing, but the winner left the more positive impression; useful but his limitations are likely to be evident again.

runners.breeder: Alban Chevalier Du Fau & Emmanuel Cheval
runners.comment: Asserted from Macho Man at Fairyhouse; brings an unblemished record but not the best form
runners.name: Proactif
runners.spotlight: Asserted in good style at Auteuil (2m2f, very soft) in September; did so by 2l from stablemate Macho Man on run-in at Fairyhouse (yielding) in January, having helped to dispute the lead; it looks like he'll come up this stiff finish well; also brings an unblemished record but not the best form.

runners.comment: Best saw him beaten 11l by Minella Study here (good to soft) in December; up against it
runners.name: Wolf Rayet
runners.spotlight: Three Flat runs in Ireland and three over hurdles in Britain; better in this sphere with three minor honours but the best of that form saw him beaten 11l by Minella Study here (good to soft) in December; met some trouble in running that day but not remotely enough to be considered a player now.

runners.comment: 3-3 and she's one of the top two on form; should have a big say if the ground is suitable
runners.name: Highland Crystal
runners.spotlight: Dam half-sister to Gold Cup contender Envoi Allen; easy winner at Punchestown (heavy) and proved much the strongest after the final flight in Listed fillies' event at Newbury (soft) later in November; got loose on the way to the start on her third intended outing but made it a perfect 3-3 record two weeks later when making most to score at Naas (soft to heavy); the challenger she saw off last time was Tuesday's 4yo handicap winner Saratoga and this filly is one of the top two on form in this contest; stays well and should have a big say if the ground is suitable.

runners.comment: Strongly run race at this trip may prove a better fit, but lots to find on the figures
runners.name: Noemie De La Vis
runners.spotlight: Runner-up at Compiegne (2m, very soft) last April and lost out in the final strides when 4-7 in a mares' maiden at Fairyhouse (2m4f, soft) eight weeks ago; looked headstrong in the latter, which soon took her to the lead and she looked certain to win before losing momentum at the final flight, but the winner was beaten 15l in a Listed race next time; strongly run race at this trip may prove a better fit but she has lots to find on the figures.

runners.breeder: Jacques Cypres & Cte G De Saint Seine
runners.comment: French winner who shaped very nicely when second in Leopardstown Grade 1 on Mullins debut
runners.name: Selma De Vary
runners.spotlight: Ran twice on Flat in France and three times in hurdle races at Auteuil, culminating in a win in November (2m2f, heavy); 17-2 and hooded again (but without the tongue-tie) at Leopardstown (2m, heavy) last month in the Grade 1 won by Narciso Has but this filly caught the eye too, held up a detached last before cutting through the field two out and keeping on into second of seven; that makes her one of the form picks in this field, in the absence of Narciso Has, and that was a promising Mullins debut.

runners.breeder: Haras De LHotellerie Meridian Int Seb
runners.comment: Two smooth wins but put firmly in her place behind Maestro Conti over C&D last time
runners.name: Tenter Le Tout
runners.spotlight: Won smoothly on good to soft at Exeter and Chepstow (Grade 2) on first two hurdle starts, but the latter was only a five-runner race and the market leaders flopped; 9-1 when beaten 13l by Maestro Conti in C&D Grade 2 (soft) seven weeks ago, so would need the ground as a major excuse to have even a squeak in this top race.

14:00.race_name: William Hill County Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Strong record in top handicap hurdles but current mark demands a big career best
runners.name: Ndaawi
runners.spotlight: Very smart hurdler whose two visits to this meeting have produced a third in the 2024 Fred Winter and second to Kargese in this last year; improved again to win last summer's Galway Hurdle (pipped by Helvic Dream but awarded the race after suffering interference); below par when remote third to Lossiemouth in Grade 1 Morgiana in November but warmed up for this with a fine run on AW Flat last month over a trip short of his best; while his good record in top handicap hurdles (also second in 2024 Galway Hurdle) makes him a dangerous one to discount, he'll require a high-class performance to win off 156.

runners.comment: Won this in 2024 and third last year but he's a good bit higher in weights now
runners.name: Absurde
runners.spotlight: Won this in 2024 and third last year, albeit off much lower marks; operated a little below his very best on the Flat last year, including in Australia in the autumn, which perhaps raises a few doubts as to whether he'll be able to find the career-best hurdle performance which will be needed to defy such a lofty mark.

runners.breeder: E A R L Elevage Des Loges
runners.comment: Arrives on a hat-trick after pair of big-field wins; further progress can't be ruled out
runners.name: Bowensonfire
runners.spotlight: Big improver in recent months, winning strong 2m Leopardstown handicaps at the Christmas meeting (yielding) and at the Dublin Racing Festival (heavy); will need to improve again to complete a hat-trick of big-field successes but that can't be ruled out in his current mood.

runners.comment: Shaped well on reappearance; Townend rides; of major interest in his first handicap
runners.name: Karbau
runners.spotlight: Smart novice hurdler last season (placed in Grade 1s) and, although defeated at short odds, produced a career-best RPR when 1l second in 2m Naas Grade 3 (heavy) on return from nine months off; entitled to build on that effort and is of major interest in his first handicap, with Paul Townend seemingly preferring him to Murcia and Absurde.

runners.comment: Grade 1 juvenile winner; not disgraced in two runs this winter; could go well
runners.name: Hello Neighbour
runners.spotlight: This useful Flat performer was a Grade 1-winning juvenile hurdler last season; sustained an injury over the summer but there's been enough in two comeback runs at Leopardstown this winter (seventh to Bowensonfire in handicap latest) to think he retains his ability; not discounted.

runners.comment: Progressive; made all in hot race at Ascot in December; second in another at Windsor since
runners.name: Wilful
runners.spotlight: Progressive 7yo who made it 5-11 over hurdles when making all in competitive handicap at Ascot (1m7f, good to soft) in December; backed that up when second of 14 in another valuable handicap at Windsor (2m, soft) in January; likeable but he will need more again.

runners.comment: Behind some of these at Dublin Racing Festival and refitted blinkers need to spark revival
runners.name: Pinot Gris
runners.spotlight: Two wins apiece on the Flat and over hurdles during his time with Gavin Cromwell but well beaten in a big-field handicap on the Flat and over hurdles (behind a few of these at Dublin Racing Festival) since joining current yard; the refitting of blinkers needs to help spark a revival.

runners.breeder: Sarl De Chambure Haras DEtreham Et Al
runners.comment: Raced wide when fourth at Dublin Racing Festival and could be primed for bold bid
runners.name: Murcia
runners.spotlight: Won a Grade 1 juvenile hurdle at Aintree last year before a decent effort behind Lulamba at Punchestown; lightly raced this season, but last month's fourth of 19 to Bowensonfire in 2m handicap at the Dublin Racing Festival shows she retains all her ability, particularly as being taken wide throughout may not have helped; Townend looks elsewhere this time, but still much respected.

runners.comment: Smart effort when second on 2m3f Ascot handicap debut and this sort of test could suit
runners.name: Tripoli Flyer
runners.spotlight: Smart novice hurdler last season; didn't take to fences during opening half of the current campaign but in good nick back hurdling last twice, finishing second on handicap debut at Ascot (2m3f, soft) in January; well-held seventh of 13 to Constitution Hill on AW Flat since; it's possible this sort of test could suit him.

runners.comment: Edged out Ndaawi in Galway Hurdle last year but demoted to second; off five months
runners.name: Helvic Dream
runners.owner: Mrs Caroline Hendron & Mrs M Cahill
runners.spotlight: Dual-purpose 9yo in fine form in both codes last year, including first past the post in the Galway Hurdle (demoted to second behind Ndaawi for interference); some respectable efforts on the Flat subsequently; first outing for five months.

runners.comment: Second in Dawn Run at 2025 Festival; fourth to Wodhooh at Christmas; first handicap hurdle
runners.name: Sixandahalf
runners.spotlight: Smart mare who was second in the Dawn Run novices' race over C&D at this meeting last year; ran close to her best when fourth of five to Wodhooh in Leopardstown Grade 2 (2m4f, good to yielding) over Christmas; freshened up since, ahead of this first attempt in a handicap hurdle.

runners.comment: Smart but a little below par since her reappearance; drops back in trip for handicap debut
runners.name: Jubilee Alpha
runners.spotlight: Three wins as a novice included a 2m4f Listed event here; advanced her RPR again when second in 2m5f Wincanton handicap (good; acts on soft) on reappearance in November but hasn't quite managed to reproduce that level since, despite finishing runner-up in Listed races the last twice; drops back in trip for her handicap debut.

runners.comment: Two Kempton wins this term; good fourth in Scottish County latest but more needed now
runners.name: Williethebuilder
runners.spotlight: A rare one in that he's improved since leaving Dan Skelton, winning a pair of 2m handicaps on good ground at Kempton this winter; creditable fourth of ten in the Scottish County at Musselburgh six weeks ago but it underlines that he needs to find a bit more from this career-high mark.

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras Du Lieu Des Champs
runners.comment: Needs to recapture level of Grade 2 novice win in autumn; tongue-tied back from wind op
runners.name: Sticktotheplan
runners.spotlight: Good start for Olly Murphy when showing a smart turn of foot to win Grade 2 Persian War (novice) at Chepstow (2m3f, good; hooded) in October; hasn't reproduced that in his two subsequent starts, latest when well beaten behind Wilful on Ascot handicap debut, but given a break (had wind surgery) and returns with a tongue-tie added.

runners.comment: No stranger to big handicap success but operating below his best this season
runners.name: Cracking Rhapsody
runners.owner: J D Wright & Mrs S Wright
runners.spotlight: Flagbearer for the yard, winning two Morebattles at Kelso and a Scottish Champion Hurdle at Ayr; however, he's failed to find his best form this season, including only sixth in the latest running of the Morebattle 13 days ago; respectable seventh in this last year; others are more obvious.

runners.comment: Won big handicap last year; better than result latest; could go well with headgear fitted
runners.name: Joyeuse
runners.spotlight: Impressive winner of top handicap hurdle at Newbury (2m, soft) last February; her progress has stalled since (including beaten favourite over fences in first two runs this season) but she was better than latest last of four to reopposing Ooh Betty in Ascot Grade 2 mares' hurdle (1m7f, soft) suggests, challenging when making a hash of the last; dropped another 3lb on the back of that and could have a say if reacting well to first-time headgear.

runners.comment: Impressed on Chepstow reappearance but has failed to fire since; hood back on
runners.name: Gibbs Island
runners.spotlight: Soft-ground maiden hurdle winner last season; impressed in 4yo handicap at Chepstow (2m, good) on reappearance in October but has failed to shine in his three outings since; has a hood fitted for a second time.

runners.comment: Back from a break to win on AW Flat last month but well beaten in Morebattle since
runners.name: Hamlets Night
runners.spotlight: Two wins in September and also a fine second in a conditions race here in October, all on good ground; back from a break with an AW Flat win last month, so it was a bit disappointing he couldn't make more of an impact in the Morebattle at Kelso (handicap hurdle debut) 13 days ago; hard to fancy after that.

runners.comment: Creditable efforts behind Bowensonfire in big-field handicaps but others better treated
runners.name: Balko dAnge
runners.spotlight: Won at Navan (2m, soft to heavy) in November and creditable efforts behind Bowensonfire in big-field handicaps at Leopardstown on both completed starts since; not obviously well treated, though.

runners.comment: In good form at the end of 2025 but needs improvement
runners.name: Bowmore
runners.spotlight: Front-runner who was a convincing winner under Daire McConville at Newbury (2m) in November before 11l third off this 10lb higher mark behind two well-handicapped rivals at Doncaster (2m, good to soft again) in December; off since; needs improvement.

runners.comment: Has joined Dan Skelton since last seen in the autumn; no surprise to see him go well
runners.name: Tellherthename
runners.spotlight: Useful hurdler who travelled powerfully in the lead for a long way in a 2m Carlisle chase on his reappearance in October only to fade on the run-in (found to have bled from the nose); that was his final start for Jonjo & A J O'Neill and he returns over hurdles under the care of a top yard which targets this race; no shock were he to go well.

runners.comment: Novice who is a very interesting handicap newcomer for yard with strong record in this
runners.name: Sinnatra
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner who has shown considerable promise on all five hurdle starts, including wins in a maiden at Sandown (2m, good) and novice at Warwick (2m3f, soft); brings an unexposed profile to this handicap debut for a leading stable with an excellent record in this contest; high on the list.

runners.comment: Very competitive in top handicaps last season; decent reappearance in Grade 2 last month
runners.name: Secret Squirrel
runners.spotlight: Won a valuable handicap hurdle at Windsor (2m, soft) last winter and probably would have been placed in two others but for falling at the last; showed more than enough to think he retains all of his ability when third of four to Alexei in the Grade 2 Kingwell at Wincanton (1m7f, heavy) on reappearance four weeks ago; entitled to come on for that.

runners.comment: Won mares' Grade 2 latest; third in Scottish Champion off same mark last spring
runners.name: Ooh Betty
runners.spotlight: Can make the running; inconsistent but returned to form with mares' Grade 2 win at Ascot (1m7f, soft) in January; runs off same mark as when close third to Cracking Rhapsody in Scottish Champion Hurdle at Ayr (2m, good to soft) last April; not ruled out each-way at likely big odds.

runners.comment: Reserve; easy 13l clear at Tramore on New Year's Day; low mileage so could progress again
runners.name: Captain Ryan Matt
runners.spotlight: Reserve; improved effort when coming 13l clear in 2m1f handicap at Tramore (soft; both wins there) on New Year's Day; much higher mark here but he's low mileage and could progress again.

runners.comment: Reserve; has done well in good handicaps, inc Aintree win last term and Newbury 2nd latest
runners.name: Wellington Arch
runners.spotlight: Reserve; won 2m4f handicap at last season's Aintree Grand National meeting (good to soft) before  third at Punchestown; disappointing when favourite on Windsor reappearance but back on his game when best of the rest behind Tutti Quanti in valuable 2m Newbury handicap (heavy) last month.

14:40.race_name: Mrs Paddy Power Mares' Chase (Registered As The Liberthine Mares' Chase) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Pulled up in Irish Gold Cup last time but 5-5 in chases previously; firmly in calculations
runners.name: Spindleberry
runners.spotlight: Concedes weight all round and pulled up in the Irish Gold Cup last time, though was facing a very tough task against males on that first rules attempt at 3m; unbeaten over fences previously (2m4f-2m6f, various ground) including a Grade 1 win against males at Fairyhouse last April and a Listed stroll at Doncaster in December; races prominently; firmly in calculations.

runners.comment: Runner-up in this in 2024 and went one better last year; she's the one to beat
runners.name: Dinoblue
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in this race in 2024 (soft) and went one better last year (good to soft); made mistakes when beaten on return to action at Navan in November and has since posted easy wins at Fairyhouse (Grade 3) and Naas (Listed) when heavily odds-on each time; she's the one to beat.

runners.comment: Won Grade 2 Arkle Trial here in November; probably needs a career best to run into a place
runners.name: July Flower
runners.spotlight: Made it 2-2 over fences in the Grade 2 Arkle Trial here (2m, soft) in November before finishing third in Grade 1 Racing Post Novice Chase at Leopardstown in December (2m1f, yielding; albeit no match for the first two); has won over 2m4f but faded up the hill in the 2m4f Mares' Hurdle here 12 months ago; probably needs a career-best performance if she's to run into a place.

runners.comment: Last year's Arkle runner-up who won Grade 3 at Naas in November; has an each-way shout
runners.name: Only By Night
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in the Arkle here (2m, good to soft) 12 months ago and returned from a break with a game win Grade 3 against males at Naas (2m, soft) in November; unproven at today's trip and well beaten in Grade 1 against males at Leopardstown (2m1f, yielding) in December, but was badly hampered at the second fence; has an each-way shout if seeing out the distance.

runners.comment: 4th of six in Listed mares' chase at Huntingdon last month and has bundles to find today
runners.name: All The Glory
runners.spotlight: Five-time hurdle winner who has shown some promise over fences this season but she was only fourth of six in a Listed mares' chase at Huntingdon last month and has bundles to find in today's company.

runners.comment: Easy Listed wins on both chase starts and it remains to be seen where her limitations lie
runners.name: Diva Luna
runners.spotlight: Grade 2 bumper winner who was third of 23 in the Grade 2 mares' novice hurdle here (2m1f, good to soft) last March; has easily won Listed mares' novice chases on her two outings over fences at Bangor (2m1f, soft) in November and Warwick (2m4f, soft) in December, and both of those front-running performances read well; today is a much tougher test of her credentials but she's very highly regarded and it remains to be seen where her limitations lie.

runners.comment: Completed notable h'cap double in November; rain would aid her cause now back down in trip
runners.name: Panic Attack
runners.spotlight: 10yo who has been better than ever this term, completing a notable handicap double in November in the Paddy Power Gold Cup (2m4f, soft; here) and the Coral Gold Cup (3m2f, good to soft) before easily completing a hat-trick in a Listed mares' chase (2m7f, good to soft); the drop back in trip isn't an obvious plus but rain would aid her cause and she's entitled to respect.

runners.comment: Listed runner-up on chase debut; very unexposed but another chunk of improvement is needed
runners.name: Piper Park
runners.spotlight: Point winner who left her first two rules runs miles behind when 25-1 Listed runner-up at Huntingdon (2m4f, soft) last month on her chase debut and first outing since 2024; very unexposed but today's assignment demands another massive chunk of improvement.

runners.comment: 6.5l second to Spindleberry at Doncaster and now 5lb better off; not ruled out each-way
runners.name: Telepathique
runners.spotlight: Highly progressive during last season's first chase campaign, culminating in Listed mares' win at Huntingdon (2m4f, good to soft) in February; back to her best when beaten just over 6l by Spindleberry at Doncaster (2m4f, good; Listed) in December and she's 5lb better off with the winner today; won on heavy ground over hurdles; not ruled out each-way at forecast big odds.

15:20.race_name: Albert Bartlett Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (Registered As The Spa Novices' Hurdle) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Hopes rest on whether this is more his trip, and pedigree offers mixed messages
runners.name: Doctor Du Mesnil
runners.spotlight: Made light work of Thedeviluno in his only bumper (yielding); very nearly won a big-field maiden at Leopardstown over Christmas but he was left for dead by The Passing Wife when odds of 2-5 in a small field at Punchestown (stepped up to 2m3f, heavy); hopes rest on whether this is more his trip, and pedigree offers mixed messages; first-time tongue-tie.

runners.comment: 3-3 over hurdles, including Grade 1 honours; can race freely but otherwise solid
runners.name: Doctor Steinberg
runners.spotlight: His bumper form was nothing to shout about but he's gone 3-3 over hurdles; it wasn't a strong Grade 1 he won at the Dublin Racing Festival (2m6f, heavy; won on good) but he bombed clear to win it by some 8l despite taking a firm grip, and his previous defeat of Thedeviluno looks all the better now; there's a nagging concern that his keen-going tendencies might come at a cost in this race, but other than that he's solid.

runners.comment: 2-2 over hurdles; rejected by Townend but this future chaser is an unknown quantity
runners.name: Espresso Milan
runners.spotlight: Beaten in three bumpers for Fergal O'Brien; unbeaten in two hurdles for Willie Mullins and the horse he made light work of at Thurles last time (2m6f, yielding) has since finished second in a big-field Class 2 handicap at Haydock; Paul Townend was highly complimentary about him last time but he still rides Doctor Steinberg; still, this future chaser remains an unknown quantity.

runners.comment: Third in a 2m4f Grade 1 latest despite not settling; retains plenty of potential
runners.name: Fruit De Mer
runners.spotlight: Winning 3m pointer on slow ground and second in a bumper on yielding; both hurdle runs on soft or heavy; it was a very winnable maiden he was found in November but he then ran quite well in a 2m4f Grade 1 at Naas, surprisingly staying on again for third having raced with the choke out early doors; retains potential, and especially over this trip, provided he gives himself a chance by settling.

runners.comment: Light on jumps experience but battle-hardened and very classy on the Flat
runners.name: Hipop De Loire
runners.spotlight: Near enough a year separated his two runs over hurdles, easily winning the latest when odds-on for a maiden at last year's Galway festival in July (good); light on experience in this scene but he's battle-hardened on the Flat and his third in September's Group 2 Doncaster Cup (2m2f; good to soft) advertises his class and stamina; it's unwise to put a line through him, for all that he's a 9yo (an 8yo has won this).

runners.comment: Long well regarded and came good with an easy maiden win at Naas; respected
runners.name: Jalon dOudairies
runners.spotlight: Excellent third when favourite for the 2024 Champion Bumper here; missed last season but definite signs of getting his act together over hurdles in posting an eyecatching RPR when strolling home at long odds-on in a 2m2f maiden at Naas (soft to heavy; effective on drier ground); unraced beyond an extended 2m4f but might yet prove that stamina is one of his assets; respected.

runners.comment: His wins have been at about 2m1f but there's stamina in the pedigree; a dark one
runners.name: Johnnys Jury
runners.owner: Blazing Blues Rc Hurlers On The Ditch
runners.spotlight: Had one run for Nicky Henderson; 2-2 for current yard, comfortably accounting for a notable rival (fourth in Tuesday's Fred Winter) at Exeter (good to soft) before winning easily again under a penalty at Carlisle (soft); brings a lower profile than many, having taken the back roads to Cheltenham, but he's a dark one; there is stamina in his pedigree, which is just as well when his wins have been at about 2m1f.

runners.comment: Hammered by Doctor Steinberg at Leopardstown last time but has place claims
runners.name: Kazansky
runners.spotlight: Should stay okay having won a point over 3m and a Grade 2 at Limerick over just shy of that trip; he's relying on Doctor Steinberg fluffing his lines as he was hammered by him at Leopardstown (2m6f, heavy) on latest start, but has place claims nonetheless.

runners.comment: Better than he showed at Doncaster but this is a tough assignment
runners.name: Kicour La
runners.spotlight: Won back-to-back minor races at about 2m4f at Leicester (soft/heavy) but limitations were seemingly ruthlessly exposed when the thick end of 20l behind Thedeviluno in Doncaster's Grade 2 River Don (3m, soft); better than he showed there but this is a tough assignment.

runners.comment: Third in a Grade 2 here in November; stable's 2019 winner was also a maiden
runners.name: Kings Bucks
runners.spotlight: 3m point winner kept to shorter trips thus far under rules; only his second run over hurdles when a running-on third behind No Drama This End (runner-up is also a class act) in a 2m5f Grade 2 here in November (soft) and perhaps it's best to forgive his odds-on defeat on desperately tiring ground in a maiden at Limerick last time; remains a maiden but so too was Minella Indo who won this race for the same yard in 2019; makes the shortlist.

runners.comment: Grade 2 Cheltenham winner, albeit in a race that has had little bearing on the Festival
runners.name: Kripticjim
runners.spotlight: Has left his bumper form behind over hurdles and completed his hat-trick in a 2m4f Grade 2 here on Trials' Day (first run in a tongue-tie; soft; fine on good); however, that was by the skin of his teeth and in a race that hasn't been that influential when it comes to the Festival; however he fares, he'll be a nice chaser next year.

runners.comment: 2-2 over hurdles and well thought of; respected with this longer trip a probable plus
runners.name: Mondouiboy
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in a 3m point and ran well in defeat in bumpers at top tracks before selling for £115,000 at the David Maxwell dispersal sale; has looked well above average in justifying market confidence over hurdles at Ludlow (2m5f) and Ascot (extended 2m3f; again on good to soft); Ben Pauling considers him one of his better novices; can't be taken lightly with this longer trip a probable plus.

runners.comment: 3m winner; won't be fazed by the nature of this race and needs a second look
runners.name: Moneygarrow
runners.spotlight: Point/bumper winner with course form having finished fifth to No Drama This End in a Grade 2 in November (behind King's Bucks); had wind surgery before he beat a good horse at Warwick (2m5f, good to soft) and put another in its place at Windsor when proving his stamina for 3m (soft); won't be fazed by the nature of this race and needs a second look.

runners.comment: Still unexposed and horses from this yard have delivered a career best in this race before
runners.name: Road Exile
runners.spotlight: By a Derby winner and there's lots of stamina on the dam's side of his pedigree; unraced beyond 2m2f under rules (did win a 3m point); maiden winner who was turned over at 8-11 last time, but in a messy race won by the classy Sober; he wouldn't be the first horse representing these connections to deliver a clear career best in this race.

runners.comment: On running style and most definitely on pedigree, the step up to 3m looks a major plus
runners.name: Spinningayarn
runners.spotlight: Point/bumper winner; won easily under no-nonsense rides from the front at Fairyhouse (2m4f, yielding) and Punchestown (2m3f, heavy) and now tackles his toughest test yet with a dangerously unexposed profile; on running style and most definitely on pedigree, the step up to 3m looks a major plus.

runners.comment: A big lad who impressed from the front at Newbury but this is a huge hike in class
runners.name: Swindon Village
runners.spotlight: This 6yo is a big lad with a bright future ahead of him; it's unlikely that Windsor played to his strengths when well behind Moneygarrow and he then stayed on much the best in a Newbury novice last month (extended 2m4f, soft); however, that latest race had no depth and the odds-on favourite wasn't on his game; this is a huge hike in class.

runners.comment: Exposed; finished tailed off behind Doctor Steinberg last time when 40-1
runners.name: Tackletommywoowoo
runners.spotlight: Raced 11 times over hurdles and plenty of experience is never a bad thing in this race; however, he's  won only three of those and finished tailed off behind Doctor Steinberg when 40-1 last time; tongue-tie enlisted.

runners.comment: Grade 2 winner at the trip; his trainer has had horses run well in this race
runners.name: Thedeviluno
runners.spotlight: 0-4 in bumpers but 2-3 over hurdles and wasn't seen to best effect in the defeat, when held up last in a Grade 2 at Navan that Doctor Steinberg dominated up front; it was over 2m that he accounted for the smart Skylight Hustle at Gowran and yet the further he went the better he looked in winning the 3m Grade 2 River Don at Doncaster (soft); his trainer has had horses run well in this before; major player.

runners.comment: Doesn't have a lot to find with Thedeviluno on an early-season maiden clash
runners.name: The Passing Wife
runners.spotlight: Pedigree doesn't exactly scream stamina but he did win a 3m point and his trainer believes this race will suit him; all his rules form is at up to 2m3f, over which he beat Doctor Du Mesnil in a small field at Punchestown last time (heavy); doesn't have a lot to find with Thedeviluno on an early-season maiden clash; seems able on all ground; respected.

runners.comment: Laboured last time behind Thedeviluno and he's not crying out to be backed
runners.name: The Price Of Peace
runners.spotlight: 3m point winner on soft; he was 1-6 for his novice win in December (just under 3m on good to soft) and it was a laboured effort last time behind Thedeviluno at Doncaster; he's not crying out to be backed.

runners.comment: There's stamina in his pedigree and potential in his profile; a lively outsider
runners.name: Ubatuba
runners.spotlight: 3m point winner; hit the ground running over hurdles with two clearcut wins under Ben Sutton at about 2m4f around Leicester (soft/heavy) and further advanced his form when a running-on second in a 3m Grade 2 at Haydock (good to soft); the useful winner got first run at Haydock and otherwise it could have been interesting; there's stamina in his pedigree and potential in his profile; appeals as one of the livelier outsiders.

runners.comment: Won against her own sex last time (3m) when coping best with the soft ground
runners.name: Park Princess
runners.spotlight: Record of 3-5 over hurdles; no mare has won this race but few have tried and The Big Westerner was runner-up 12 months ago; however, although a wide-margin winner at Doncaster last time (3m, soft), that was against her own sex and very few in that eight-runner race appeared to handle the conditions; reservations.

16:00.race_name: Boodles Cheltenham Gold Cup Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Three Cheltenham Festival wins but now 12 and today's task is likely to prove beyond him
runners.name: Envoi Allen
runners.spotlight: His remarkable haul of ten Grade 1 wins includes three at the Cheltenham Festival, and it was at that level that he won at Down Royal in November on his sole outing this season; however, he was a well-beaten third in the Ryanair last March and, now 12, today's task is likely to prove beyond him.

runners.comment: 14l 4th in Irish Gold Cup; he'll be doing very well if he betters that finishing position
runners.name: Firefox
runners.spotlight: He's performed respectably in defeat at the last two Cheltenham Festivals and won a Grade 2 at Down Royal (2m3f, good to yielding) in November; 14l fourth when upped in trip in the Irish Gold Cup (3m, soft) last month and he'll be doing very well if he improves upon that finishing position today.

runners.comment: String of excellent performances since Grade 1 Bowl win at Aintree last April; respected
runners.name: Gaelic Warrior
runners.spotlight: Won the Arkle here (2m, soft) in March 2024 and relished the step up to 3m1f in the Grade 1 Bowl at Aintree (good to soft) last April; that win has been the catalyst for a string of excellent efforts, including his third in a blanket finish in the King George (3m, good to soft) in December and his 5l second in the Irish Gold Cup (3m, soft) last month; can be difficult to settle which is something of a concern in view of today's stiff stamina test, but on the flip side he's been finishing his races strongly; respected.

runners.comment: Runner-up in French Grade 1 in November but this French raider would be a shock winner
runners.name: Gold Tweet
runners.spotlight: Impressive in Grade 2 Cleeve Hurdle here (3m, soft) in January 2023 and 7l runner-up in Grade 1 chase in France (3m3f, heavy) in November this term; rain would be a plus for this French raider but he was soundly beaten in the 2024 Betfair Chase on his last British start and would be a shock winner.

runners.comment: Won Grade 1 Betfair Chase at Haydock in November but may just lack the required class
runners.name: Grey Dawning
runners.spotlight: Won the 2m4f novice chase at the 2024 Festival (soft) and added a second Grade 1 win in the Betfair Chase at Haydock (3m1f, good to soft) this season; a mistake two out proved costly when 5l third of four to Spillane's Tower in the Grade 2 Cotswold Chase here (3m1f, soft) in January and he rallied up the hill; however, he may just lack the required class today.

runners.breeder: Dr V Simon Mrs V Simon & Mr N Simon
runners.comment: Highly progressive 9yo who should prove well suited to the demands of today's race
runners.name: Haiti Couleurs
runners.spotlight: Prominent-racer who won the NH Chase (Handicap) at this meeting 12 months ago (3m6f, good to soft) and bounced back from November's Betfair Chase flop to win the Welsh National (3m6f, good to soft) and also the Grade 2 Denman Chase (2m7f, heavy); this highly progressive 9yo is now 6-8 over fences and should prove well suited to the demands of today's race, all the more so if there's rain and stamina is at a premium; firmly in calculations.

runners.comment: Disappointing this season but won this by 6l last year; attracted market support last week
runners.name: Inothewayurthinkin
runners.spotlight: Disappointing on his three runs this term and a major turnaround is required; however, he's left his winter form behind to win at the Cheltenham Festival in each of the last two seasons (soft/good to soft), including this race last year by 6l, and he attracted market support last week; cheekpieces go on and he'll be tough to beat if rediscovering his brilliant best.

runners.comment: Very close 4th in King George thriller and may well improve again for today's stiffer test
runners.name: Jango Baie
runners.spotlight: Came from behind to win the Arkle here (2m, good to soft) 12 months ago and, as could be anticipated, was well suited by the step up to 3m when a very close fourth behind The Jukebox Man and Gaelic Warrior in the King George at Kempton (3m, good) in December; of the four involved in that thrilling finish he arguably shaped as the one most likely to improve for today's stiffer test; seems versatile ground-wise; could play a leading role.

runners.comment: 3-time course winner; runner-up on his three starts this term; this 11yo is up against it
runners.name: LHomme Presse
runners.spotlight: Won the Grade 1 Brown Advisory here in March 2022 and also the Cotswold Chase here last January; pushed Spillane's Tower close in that same 3m1f Grade 2 this season, when conceding 6lb to the winner, but no match for Haiti Couleurs since and this 11yo is up against it in today's company.

runners.comment: Won the Grade 2 Cotswold Chase here in January but needs an even bigger performance today
runners.name: Spillanes Tower
runners.spotlight: Won two Grade 1s in Ireland in spring 2024 during novice chase campaign (2m4f/3m1f, heavy/yielding) and posted first win since in the Grade 2 Cotswold Chase here (3m1f, soft) this January; only eight and it's possible he has an even bigger performance in him, but he had to work hard last time and was receiving 6lb from the runner-up L'Homme Presse; others preferred.

runners.comment: Rallied for narrow win in breathtaking King George; 4-4 over fences and he's a key player
runners.name: The Jukebox Man
runners.spotlight: Cruelly caught in the final strides in the Albert Bartlett Novices' Hurdle here (3m, heavy) in March 2024; 2-2 in novice chases last season (including Grade 1) and, after missing last year's Festival due to injury, he made it 2-2 this term and 4-4 over fences when winning the King George (3m, good) in December, narrowly in a breathtaking four-way finish (Gaelic Warrior third, Jango Baie fourth); the way he rallied to edge back in front at Kempton provides optimism regarding today's stiffer test and he's a key player.

16:40.race_name: Princess Royal Challenge Cup Open Hunters' Chase

runners.comment: Could run well for a long way but ultimately prove vulnerable to stronger stayers
runners.name: Barton Snow
runners.spotlight: Winner here at last May's hunter chase meeting but that was over 2m; his 3m point wins came chiefly in small-field affairs and he was left clear late on when successful over that trip at Ludlow on latest start, and the time was ordinary; could run well for a long way but ultimately prove vulnerable to stronger stayers.

runners.comment: Ran well for a 100-1 shot in this last year (sixth); another notable run at Christmas
runners.name: Carnfunnock
runners.spotlight: Ran well for a 100-1 shot in this last year (sixth), doing all his best work late in the day; that was also the case when only 6l off Its On The Line at Down Royal over Christmas and, like last year, he arrives here after winning a point; cheekpieces offered nothing when tried once before but that was over hurdles; place possibilities.

runners.comment: Formerly smart and his autumn point wins may have given him some renewed belief
runners.name: Chemical Energy
runners.spotlight: Won a novice chase here in October 2022 and was second in the National Hunt Chase at this fixture later that season; on a losing run of 14 under rules but he's contested plenty of strong handicaps in that time and back-to-back point wins in the autumn may give him some renewed belief; has soft-ground form but his trainer has always believed that good ground is ideal, so watch the weather; well held in a Galway Plate when previously tried in this equipment combination.

runners.comment: An up-and-coming 9yo with so few runs on the board; a likely improver over this far
runners.name: Cons Roc
runners.spotlight: An up-and-coming 9yo with so few runs on the board; 2-4 in points and suffered his first defeat in hunter chases when a rallying third behind Its On The Line and Willitgoahead at Down Royal during the Christmas period; he was favourite that day; this greater emphasis on stamina promises to play to his strengths; good chance in first-time cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Useful handicapper and 2-2 in hunter chases; could have a say if he sees out the trip
runners.name: Golden Son
runners.owner: G Mason A Ferguson And P Nicholls
runners.spotlight: Talented 2m4f/3m handicapper who has returned from ten months off to win hunter chases at Warwick (3m, good to soft) and Taunton (2m7f, heavy); he wasn't remotely pressed on either occasion and the RPRs were highly respectable; Paul Nicholls has won this four times and this 8yo could be interesting, provided he lasts home.

runners.comment: Won last year's hunter chase at Aintree's big meeting and has C&D form
runners.name: Gracchus De Balme
runners.spotlight: Only last April he enjoyed his finest hour when winning the hunters' chase over the Grand National fences (good to soft); followed that with a second over C&D to Music Drive before winning Stratford's Horse & Hound Cup; he's not without hope judged on all that and, although this year's form is underwhelming, so too was his run prior to winning at Aintree.

runners.comment: All roads have led to this after narrow defeats in the last three runnings; clear chance
runners.name: Its On The Line
runners.spotlight: Part of the furniture in this race after going agonisingly close in the last three runnings, especially 12 months ago when he stayed on strongly to push Wonderwall to a neck, after which he secured a repeat win at Punchestown; although it's hardly encouraging that he was turned over at 1-5 in his latest point, the winner is useful on his day and this 9yo didn't exactly arrive here 12 months ago with the wind in his sails; all roads have led to this and he has clear claims.

runners.breeder: Mme Sophie Bouchet Lardot Et Al
runners.comment: He's only 1-8 over regulation fences and doesn't look up to this at the age of 12
runners.name: King Alex
runners.spotlight: Has been running well in points, though was grossly flattered by his close proximity to Wonderwall in November; he's only 1-8 over regulation fences and doesn't look up to this at the age of 12.

runners.comment: Point/hunter chase winner; only a 6yo but this race looks too tough
runners.name: Kings Jet
runners.spotlight: Won a hunter chase last May (on good ground) and probably wasn't in love with the heavy surface (has won on yielding to soft) when tailed off behind Con's Roc at Fairyhouse in November in his latest hunter chase; has since run well behind a prolific pointer; only a 6yo but this race looks too tough.

runners.comment: Tailed off in this last year (33-1); credentials are no more compelling this time around
runners.name: Lift Me Up
runners.spotlight: Jumping failed the test when he was tailed off in this last year, going off at 33-1, and his credentials are no more compelling this time around.

runners.comment: 1st and 2nd in hunter chases; back from a break to beat Music Drive in a point in January
runners.name: Linelee King
runners.spotlight: This is his first visit to Cheltenham since beating one home in the Champion Bumper six years ago; has won one of his two hunter chases and the Cartmel defeat came at the hands of a useful rival; back from a break to beat Music Drive readily in a point in January and he could run well at lengthy odds; effective on good to soft and slower ground.

runners.comment: Beaten in his recent point; a repeat of last year's fourth in this would be a result
runners.name: Music Drive
runners.spotlight: Eighth in the 2022 Champion Bumper and twice placed over hurdles here when with Gordon Elliott; has done well for current team following a long absence, winning over C&D last May after his never-dangerous 13l fourth to Wonderwall in this 12 months ago; he'll need to get his skates on a bit earlier to improve on that placing and he was beaten by Linelee King in a recent point (after a long break admittedly); the return of cheekpieces is no bad thing; seems fine on all ground.

runners.comment: Former classy chaser and back in the good books after his recent hunter chase wins
runners.name: Panda Boy
runners.spotlight: Has always had some class about him and he went off only 11-1 for the Grand National two seasons ago; lost his way afterwards but he's back in the good books after winning two hunter chases and the RPR he posted at Naas last month (3m, heavy; fine on good ground) was up there with his best; with confidence seemingly buoyed he's a must for the shortlist.

runners.comment: Held by Golden Son in January and he was entitled to win his last two races at odds-on
runners.name: Paul Marvel
runners.owner: N&k Richards L&b Doyle M&k Shore
runners.spotlight: Beaten 6l by Golden Son at Warwick in January and his subsequent wins (in the new cheekpieces) were races he was entitled to win at odds-on; lacks Cheltenham experience; opposable.

runners.comment: Dual hunter chase winner but tends to struggle on the bigger stage
runners.name: Pyleigh Court
runners.spotlight: Dual hunter chase winner but tends to struggle on the bigger stage, as when a remote third on his one visit here (2023) and pulled up in the Aintree Foxhunters' last April.

runners.comment: In the firing line throughout when fifth last year; can improve on his third at Haydock
runners.name: Shearer
runners.spotlight: Relinquished an unbeaten record over regulation fences when fifth in this race last year, though he did well to be only 13l off Wonderwall given that he was in the firing line throughout; it's best not to read too much into a recent odds-on defeat behind past Festival hero Unexpected Party at Haydock (2m6f) as that was probably needed after 11 months off; has no ground preferences; can run well.

runners.comment: Stamina queries over this far but his trainer has won this three times; visor is new
runners.name: Solitary Man
runners.spotlight: Only an 8yo; he'll need to run better than when 17l fourth behind Panda Boy at Thurles in January but the market expected better of him and in his subsequent point he beat Winged Leader, who nearly won this in 2022; there are stamina queries over this far but his trainer has won this three times, so he knows what's required; first-time visor; seems able on all ground.

runners.comment: Past Festival winner; strong stayer who could be running on when others have cried enough
runners.name: Stattler
runners.spotlight: A guaranteed stayer having won the 3m6f National Hunt Chase at this meeting four years ago when in the care of Willie Mullins, for whom he signed off when pulled up in the Grand National of 2024; remains in the same ownership; back from a long absence with competitive shows in hunter chases at Hereford and Fakenham; cheekpieces added; all ground comes alike to him; could be running on when others have cried enough.

runners.comment: Going okay when falling three out last year; returns after a pleasing run at Haydock
runners.name: Take All
runners.spotlight: 125-1 for this last year but was still travelling within himself when falling three out; returns on the back of a positive performance at Haydock when just ahead of Shearer; hood returns; he's no forlorn hope by any means.

runners.comment: Never counted in this 12 months ago and returns a year older and in no better form
runners.name: What A Glance
runners.spotlight: Winner at this track in 2024 and he then beat Lift Me Up in Stratford's Horse & Hound Cup; however, he never counted in this 12 months ago and returns a year older and in no better form.

runners.comment: Gracchus De Balme and Linelee King have had his measure in the past
runners.name: Willewonga
runners.spotlight: Five-time point winner but turned over at odds-on in latest start in that sphere; Gracchus De Balme and Linelee King have had his measure in the past.

runners.comment: 3rd in 2025; eight is no age in this discipline; there's a suspicion he has more to give
runners.name: Willitgoahead
runners.spotlight: Took his form to a new level in hunter chases last season and was recruited by these connections prior to finishing a staying-on third in this 12 months ago; that campaign ended on a low note and, as in this last year, Its On The Line was ahead of him on his comeback at Down Royal; unseated mid-race last time; he needs a career best but eight is no age in this discipline and there's a suspicion he has more to give.

runners.comment: Won this last year and returns fresh after a strikingly similar preparation
runners.name: Wonderwall
runners.spotlight: Has gone 4-4 since being bought for £33,000 in July 2024 and he emerged from midfield to win this last year (good to soft; effective on softer), fending off the late charge of Its On The Line; has undergone a similar preparation, arriving here fresh after winning a point in early November; there have been back-to-back winners of this race and a bold defence looks on the cards.

runners.comment: Looked good in winning two points this winter; similar profile to yard's winner last year
runners.name: Wrappedupinmay
runners.spotlight: Promising hurdler for Paul Nicholls, later sold on for £14,000 after two comprehensive failures over fences; however, he's looked good in winning two slow-ground points for Sam Curling and his profile isn't entirely dissimilar to that which his stablemate Wonderwall brought prior to winning this last year; he gives his yard a useful second string to their bow.

17:20.race_name: Martin Pipe Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.breeder: Mrs Nicole Capelli Dambrine Et Al
runners.comment: Made a winning handicap debut (2m) last time; possibilities provided he stays the new trip
runners.name: Its Bilbo
runners.spotlight: Campaigned only at about 2m; made a successful handicap debut in Limerick contest (soft to heavy; Listed) on last appearance, proving suited by the return to hurdles after two chase defeats; this 5yo looks open to further improvement and has possibilities provided he stays the new trip.

runners.comment: Useful mare; 6-12 over hurdles and dual C&D scorer; only midfield in this race last year
runners.name: Nurse Susan
runners.spotlight: Useful mare whose record of 6-12 over hurdles includes two handicap wins over C&D and Listed honours at Sandown; heavy ground possibly contributed to a form-dip last time; faded into midfield in this race last year but was ridden more prominently than usual; on a stiffer mark this time.

runners.comment: May raise her game returned to Cheltenham; Grade 2 winner at this meeting 12 months ago
runners.name: Air Of Entitlement
runners.spotlight: Stays 2m4f; got up close home in the Grade 2 novice hurdle for mares at this meeting 12 months ago (2m1f, good to soft); no further progress in three starts since, disappointing in Listed handicap latest, but may raise her game returned to the Cheltenham Festival; not ruled out.

runners.breeder: The Hon Mrs V M A Tower
runners.comment: Well treated on best chase form but has never been able to show it over hurdles
runners.name: Sa Fureur
runners.spotlight: Well treated on best chase form, including second in Gowran Grade 2 when returned to that sphere last time, but he has never been able to show it over hurdles; his Cheltenham Festival record of P40, the fourth-place finish over fences, adds to the uncertainty.

runners.comment: Switches back to hurdles from chasing; faces a stiff assignment in this field
runners.name: Farfromnowhere
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 8yo; switched to chasing in last two appearances, looking a non-stayer over 2m6f latest; registered comfortable wins in non-handicaps over hurdles (2m3f/2m4f) in 2024 and 2025 but faces a stiffer assignment off a mark of 138 in this deeper field; tongue-tie applied.

runners.comment: Returns to hurdles after a spell over fences; 0-13 since debut win and looks exposed
runners.name: Karl Des Tourelles
runners.spotlight: Has failed to match the pick of his hurdles form since switched to fences; last two attempts in this sphere resulted in creditable efforts in notable staying handicaps last spring, including in the Pertemps Final at this meeting; quite exposed, however, and is 0-13 since debut win.

runners.comment: Has registered both hurdles wins over 2m; still needs to prove he stays 2m4f
runners.name: Zillow
runners.spotlight: Has registered both hurdles wins over 2m, including in Listed handicap at Fairyhouse in November; early faller at the Dublin Racing Festival last time; something to prove back up in distance, having failed to convince with his stamina in three attempts at about 2m4f.

runners.comment: Lightly raced 6yo who may improve sharply on his Grade 3 efforts this term; interesting
runners.name: Kel Histoire
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 6yo who had form figures of 112 prior to a stiffer task (well held) in the Turners at this meeting last year; faces a more suitable assignment returned to Cheltenham and may improve sharply on his couple of fifth-place finishes at Grade 3 level (2m) this term; interesting.

runners.comment: Won at Ascot upped to 2m3f last time; unexposed at this sort of trip; has Cheltenham form
runners.name: Fiercely Proud
runners.spotlight: Has gained both handicap wins in useful races at Ascot, including latest start when upped to 2m3f (good to soft) and back to best; back on career-high mark but is unexposed at this sort of trip and not necessarily track dependent; has bits of Cheltenham form, including a bumper success.

runners.comment: Respectable seventh (best of the runners who raced prominently) in this contest last year
runners.name: East India Express
runners.spotlight: Best on good/good to soft; has notable C&D form, namely a respectable seventh (best of the runners who raced prominently) in this contest last year and emphatic success next time; unlucky second at Windsor on New Year's Day when last seen; back on career-high mark but looks solid.

runners.comment: Placed over fences on last two runs; needs to prove he can still show best hurdles form
runners.name: Da Capo Glory
runners.spotlight: Back in better form with placed efforts over fences on last two starts; fairly useful hurdler on his day and ran respectably (finished seventh) off a higher mark in the 2m5f handicap at this meeting two years ago; however, whether he retains that level of ability is not fully clear.

runners.comment: Needs to prove he's still capable of reproducing best Irish form; second run for new yard
runners.name: Intellotto
runners.spotlight: Flat and jumps winner for Joseph O'Brien; ran according to market expectations (rank outsider of four) in the Kingwell Hurdle on return from layoff and debut for new stable; drops back in class but needs to prove he's still capable of reproducing best Irish form.

runners.comment: Cracking effort in this race last year, beating all bar smart Wodhooh; only 1lb higher
runners.name: Act Of Authority
runners.spotlight: Hasn't won since November 2024 but he's a broadly consistent sort and posted a cracking effort in this race (good to soft) 12 months ago, beating all bar smart mare Wodhooh who was very well handicapped; only 1lb higher and again has each-way possibilities; wears first-time headgear.

runners.comment: Made eye-catching late headway in sole 2m4f attempt (penultimate start); has potential
runners.name: Wendrock
runners.spotlight: Only 1-10 over hurdles but shaped very well, making eye-catching late headway from a difficult position, in Listed handicap at Leopardstown (good to yielding; penultimate start) on sole 2m4f attempt and only outing under Carl Millar; interesting contender who has potential at this trip.

runners.comment: Solid record as hurdler; ran well in Graded races over C&D and at Thurles on last two runs
runners.name: Open Secret
runners.spotlight: Acts on any ground; solid record (42142) since joining current stable and switched to hurdles, running well in Grade 2 over C&D and Grade 3 at Thurles (2m5f) on last two starts; latter race threw up the winners of this contest, for this yard, in 2017 and 2018; good credentials.

runners.comment: Bred to be suited by this trip; still open to further progress; 1-1 under Josh Williamson
runners.name: Stede Bonnet
runners.spotlight: Dual bumper/hurdles winner over 2m/2m1f, most recently at Ayr in January; steadily run Listed race didn't pan out favourably last time; bred to be suited by this new trip on handicap debut, remains open to further progress and is 1-1 under Josh Williamson; reasons to be positive.

runners.comment: Progressive last term; recent success in a Flat challenge race confirms his wellbeing
runners.name: Jump Allen
runners.spotlight: Progressive novice hurdler last term, culminating in Sandown handicap success (2m4f, good); followed up in Flat challenge race at Punchestown last month, holding on from main market rival and confirming his wellbeing ahead of this return to jumps; may have more to offer.

runners.comment: Record of 321 since handicapping; improving and remains particularly unexposed beyond 2m
runners.name: Andashan
runners.spotlight: Record of 321 switched to handicaps this term and the form has substance; ran well behind a notable rival on penultimate start (2m3f, good to soft) and subsequent Newbury performance (2m4f, good) took his strike-rate to 3-9; improving and remains particularly unexposed beyond 2m.

runners.comment: Consistent in Ireland this term for Donncha Duggan; stiffer task on debut for new yard
runners.name: Ballykinlar
runners.spotlight: Consistent form in Ireland this season for Donncha Duggan features three summer wins; absent since finishing second in Listed novice event at Limerick (2m5f, yielding) five months ago; appears to have a stiffer task on debut for new connections but market support should be noted.

runners.comment: Recorded a career-best RPR with game win over 3m most recently; peaking at the right time
runners.name: Saint Le Fort
runners.spotlight: Peaking at the right time, having recorded a career-best RPR with game win under Niall Moore in Listed handicap at Leopardstown (3m, heavy) last month; however, doesn't seem to be crying out for this drop back in trip.

runners.comment: Runner-up in two races won by notable rivals since joining Willie Mullins; respected
runners.name: Roc Dino
runners.spotlight: Ex-French, five-race maiden who has shown consistent promise; runner-up in 2m events won by notable rivals, who both contested the Supreme here on Tuesday, since joining Willie Mullins; open to progress now handicapping over a new trip and could be very well treated off this mark; respected.

runners.comment: Failed to complete on last two starts; difficult to support on second run for new yard
runners.name: Charlus
runners.spotlight: Failed to complete on his last two runs, falling on final start for Willie Mullins then pulled up in 2m5f handicap when 66-1 for new yard; with those letters next to his name, he cannot be supported confidently in a race of this depth; tongue-tie added.

runners.comment: Fairly useful hurdler at about 2m; goes into unknown territory over this longer distance
runners.name: Hot Fuss
runners.spotlight: Fairly useful hurdler at about 2m and ran creditably (lost two places close home; finished fourth) in the Fred Winter at this meeting 12 months ago; bagged a valuable pot at Windsor (soft) in January but form dipped last time; goes into unknown territory over this longer distance.

runners.breeder: Terrains DAvilly St Leonard Et Al
runners.comment: Disappointing mare; chance depends on whether new trip has positive effect
runners.name: Sainte Lucie
runners.spotlight: Campaigned only at about 2m; disappointing mare who has unconvincing form figures since scoring easily on debut for Willie Mullins; posted duck eggs in competitive handicaps at Leopardstown on last two outings; new trip needs to make a big difference.

runners.comment: Reserve; may show progress with cheekpieces retained in this second handicap attempt
runners.name: He Cant Dance
runners.spotlight: Reserve; point/bumper winner who has broadly consistent hurdles form over 2m5f-3m, most recently 15l third to Saint Le Fort at Leopardstown (heavy) with cheekpieces added on handicap debut; may show progress in the retained headgear, provided he copes with this drop back in distance.

runners.comment: Reserve; no further progress since reappearance win; faces a difficult assignment
runners.name: Glynn Brae
runners.spotlight: Reserve; has a respectable overall strike-rate (5-11) but has seemingly reached reached his ceiling, having failed to make any further progress since the most recent success, which was gained at Sandown (2m4f) on seasonal debut; faces a difficult assignment.
